title: Coherent realization of fixed-vertex inclusions is a fixed-object cofibration
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the subset-poset coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Let $u:K\to L$ be a degreewise injective map of small simplicial sets inducing a bijection $u_0:K_0\to L_0$. Put $O=K_0$ and identify the vertex set of $L$ with $O$ by $u_0^{-1}$. Let $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ be the category of simplicial categories with object set $O$ and simplicial functors equal to the identity on $O$. It has the fixed-object model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]: weak equivalences and fibrations are detected on each mapping simplicial set. A cofibration here means a map having the left lifting property against every functor whose mapping-set maps are trivial Kan fibrations; trivial means a Kan fibration that is also a weak homotopy equivalence. A Kan fibration is a map having the right lifting property against every horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$. Left lifting means a diagonal making both triangles commute in every commutative square. Then the induced functor $\mathfrak C[u]:\mathfrak C[K]\to\mathfrak C[L]$, considered in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$, is a cofibration. No quasicategory or local Kan hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, first paragraph of its proof, printed p. 90 (PDF p. 107): the coherent boundary is the boundary of the (n-1)-cube for n>0; fixed-object cofibrations are the free boundary extensions of Appendix A.3.2. Only the initial cofibration calculation is used, before any Joyal model existence or Quillen equivalence. No Stacks tag states this simplicial enriched result. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Identify $K$ with its image in $L$. By [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], write $K=Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq L$ with union $L$, where stage $n$ attaches precisely the missing nondegenerate $n$-simplices along their boundaries. Since $K_0=L_0$, the set of missing $0$-simplices is empty and $Z_1=Z_0$. All remaining cells have $n\geq1$ and all stages have the same vertex set $O$. This is the dimension filtration, so boundaries, including degenerate faces, already lie in the preceding stage.

source.place: Opening paragraph of the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1; relative skeletal presentation also Kerodon Tag 0077, proof of Proposition 1.5.5.14(b).

proof.text: The colimit definition in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] gives a direct universal-property check that $\mathfrak C$ preserves these pushouts and their sequential colimit. For any small simplicial category $D$, put $N(D)_m=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(\mathfrak C[\Delta^m],D)$, with operators by precomposition. A functor $\mathfrak C[S]\to D$ is exactly a family of simplex functors indexed by $\Delta^m\to S$, compatible with all monotone operators, hence exactly a simplicial map $S\to N(D)$. A compatible family of maps from a simplicial colimit into $N(D)$ is exactly a map from that colimit. Applying these two bijections proves the required enriched colimit assertions. The object set of $\mathfrak C[S]$ is $S_0$: in its simplex presentation the object identifications are exactly the vertex identifications, and composition adds only arrows. Consequently each realized stage has object set $O$. The colimit universal property restricts to functors fixing $O$, since their object functions all equal the identity. No assertion that individual mapping sets preserve these colimits is used.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, first paragraph; universal-property expansion of the coherent-realization definition of Section 1.1.5.

proof.text: Consider an arbitrary square against a simplicial functor $p:E\to F$ in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ whose mapping maps are trivial Kan fibrations. For one attached $n$-simplex $\sigma$, let its vertices have labels $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in O$, allowing repetitions. Restrict the already constructed top functor along $\mathfrak C[\partial\sigma]$ to $g:\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]\to E$, and the bottom functor along $\mathfrak C[\sigma]$ to $f:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to F$; then $p\circ g$ is the restriction of $f$. By [lem-coef-rigidification-boundary-cube], with $B_{n-1}=(\Delta^1)^{n-1}$ and $\partial B_{n-1}$ its union of coordinate faces, $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ is the pushout of $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]$ and $U(B_{n-1})$ over $U(\partial B_{n-1})$, the two objects of $U$ going to $0$ and $n$. Hence a functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to E$ extending $g$ is exactly a simplicial map $B_{n-1}\to E(a_0,a_n)$ whose restriction to $\partial B_{n-1}$ is the forward mapping map $\partial B_{n-1}\to E(a_0,a_n)$ of $g$ composed with the top horizontal functor; and by the uniqueness in the pushout such an extension lies over $f$ exactly when its cube map composed with $p$ is the forward cube map $B_{n-1}\to F(a_0,a_n)$ of $f$. The remaining requirement is therefore a square of simplicial sets $\partial B_{n-1}\to E(a_0,a_n)$ over $B_{n-1}\to F(a_0,a_n)$, with left map the inclusion. Coinciding labels change nothing: the pushout is formed in $\mathrm{sCat}$ with arbitrary object functions, and a functor $U(K)\to E$ sending both objects to one $a$ is just a map $K\to E(a,a)$, since $U(K)$ has identity mapping sets $\Delta^0$ and empty mapping set from $1$ to $0$.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, first paragraph, the explicit mapping-set calculation and its free extension interpretation (pushout along U of the cube boundary).

proof.text: The inclusion $\partial B_{n-1}\hookrightarrow B_{n-1}$ is degreewise injective, including $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$ when $n=1$. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], it is a Kan-Quillen cofibration, while $E(a_0,a_n)\to F(a_0,a_n)$ is a trivial fibration for exactly the weak homotopy equivalences and horn fibrations in the item. The model lifting axiom therefore supplies a diagonal cube map $B_{n-1}\to E(a_0,a_n)$ extending the prescribed map on $\partial B_{n-1}$ and lying over the cube map of $f$. By the pushout of step 3 it and $g$ define an enriched functor on $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, agreeing with $g$ on $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]$ and lying over $f$. No fibrancy of $E(a,b)$ or $F(a,b)$ as objects is required.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, first paragraph; the Kan-Quillen cofibration/trivial-fibration lifting axiom, Hovey Theorem 3.6.5.

proof.text: Start the induction with the specified functor $h_0:\mathfrak C[K]\to E$. Suppose $h_n$ has been constructed over $F$. For each cell in the small set indexing stage $n$, choose the extension from steps 3 and 4, with its boundary prescribed by $h_n$. These extensions and $h_n$ agree on the attaching coproduct. The pushout universal property proved in step 2 supplies $h_{n+1}:\mathfrak C[Z_{n+1}]\to E$ restricting to $h_n$ and commuting with $p$. The empty stage $n=0$ uses $h_1=h_0$. At the sequential colimit, the compatible $h_n$ give $h:\mathfrak C[L]\to E$. Both triangle equations hold on every stage, hence on the colimit by its universal property. All maps fix $O$, so $h$ is a diagonal in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. This proves the asserted left lifting property.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, first paragraph; explicit induction and colimit verification of the lifting property.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_fixed_vertex_cofibrations {K L : SSet.{u}} (f : K ⟶ L) (hinj : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (f.app n)) (hvertices : Function.Bijective (f.app (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌))) : ∃ (A B : Bergner.Fixed (K _⦋0⦌)) (eK : Bergner.bundle A ≅ rigidification.obj K) (eL : Bergner.bundle B ≅ rigidification.obj L) (g : A ⟶ B), (∀ x : K _⦋0⦌, eK.hom.obj x = (coherentSimplexUnit.app ⦋0⦌ ≫ rigidification.map (yonedaEquiv.symm x)).obj (SimplicialThickening.mk (ULift.up 0))) ∧ (∀ x : K _⦋0⦌, eL.hom.obj x = (coherentSimplexUnit.app ⦋0⦌ ≫ rigidification.map (yonedaEquiv.symm (f.app _ x))).obj (SimplicialThickening.mk (ULift.up 0))) ∧ Bergner.bundleMap g ≫ eL.hom = eK.hom ≫ rigidification.map f ∧ Bergner.fixedCofibrations (K _⦋0⦌) g

No additional definition or mathematical hypothesis.
